Example: the active account has lost its subscription, and the other account has a soft 5h stop of 50% at 60% usage, still under the 98 threshold. pick_target_with would switch through the stage at src/usage.rs:321-326. This path returns NoCandidate, so the user stays on an account that cannot be used at all.

An account whose usage cannot be fetched (for example a revoked token) becomes a silent 'throttled' fallback target with arbitrarily old numbers on the ticks after its failure. This contradicts README.md:179, which says only accounts the API throttles may count with old numbers. The log at lib.rs:2533 also calls it a 'gemeinsame API-Pause'.

A user who pinned an account by hand reads that the pin behaves as before. The service will in fact switch away from it once the profile endpoint reports the subscription inactive. docs/usage-gate.md:15 states the exception, so README and docs give two different rules for the same behaviour.

`claude-account ping` and the web action /api/actions/ping (src/web.rs:467-469) can send a second ping into a quota whose earlier ping confirmation is still pending. That spends quota and starts another unconfirmed run, while the docs promise this cannot happen.
`claude-account --help` tells the user the command opens the window immediately, then the command fails with an error. User-facing text misstates behaviour.

The command reference and CLI help describe a switch only at a full limit. A user running `claude-account auto` at 93%, or on an account whose subscription has lapsed, gets a switch the reference says will not happen. Only the prose at README:181 mentions the reserve trigger.
The regression that justifies hook finding 23 (subprocess latency) is not guarded, and the doc presents a test that cannot fail as verification.
The test does not pin the readiness guard it is cited for; the finding-28 class stays unguarded.
Two documents in the same release disagree about confirmation release and pin precedence. A reader of RELEASE.md misjudges when jobs and pings unblock and when pins are overridden.

A paid account in a past_due grace period with has_claude_max=true is marked inactive. It then loses cached usage (src/lib.rs:2203), is excluded as a target and overrides pins (src/lib.rs:1824), and stays inactive until a positive check, while the doc says it would not be. Either the rule or the doc is wrong; they cannot both stand.
This twin of the shared-settings duplication class (findings 21/29) is unfixed. Changing one site leaves predictive_switch and projected_usage disagreeing on when a measurement can drive prediction.
The doc misstates runtime behaviour, and this repeated-error twin (findings 22/25/33) is left unfixed, flooding the journal.

During a store-wide 429 cooldown (300-900 s plus Retry-After up to 24 h), the active reading ages past 20 minutes. An operator relying on the document expects a switch at limit minus reserve (93 % by default), but the switcher waits until 98 %. That is exactly the throttled scenario this change targets.

Changing one 1200 without the other splits the measured-fallback gate from the slope gate: a reading could pass one and fail the other, silently changing when reserve protection applies. The task record's claim of a single definition is false.

If a reader holds the lock while run_job_now runs, run_job_now bails with 'Es laeuft bereits eine Aufgabe' (src/lib.rs:2870-2871). If it holds the lock during the watcher tick, the watcher logs 'Aufgaben warten: es laeuft bereits eine' and skips starting a due job (src/lib.rs:3434-3436). Both report a running job that does not exist. The lock is an fs2 flock, so this also applies within one process.

One unreadable profile or one failed job write while any job is pending makes every job reader fail: web_snapshot (500), job list, status and job add. The watcher falls back to an empty list (src/lib.rs:3380-3384), so no job runs, including jobs without a pending confirmation, and log_problem repeats every tick. The ping twin isolates the same bookkeeping (src/lib.rs:3494-3503), and c3bd0fa claims that isolation.

The ping twin checks expiry inside the shared predicate (src/lib.rs:4717-4721). For jobs, an expired confirmation keeps blocking whenever the loader missed the lock, so README.md:261 ('endet die Sperre spätestens nach fünf Stunden') depends on caller timing. No test reaches this guard.

Scenario: a repeat job runs on account A, the watcher switches to B mid-run (it keeps running during jobs, src/lib.rs:3458-3460), and the job opens B's window. last_window becomes A's reset, B's reset differs, and 15 min later the job runs again inside the B window it just used. This contradicts the documented rule at src/jobs.rs:236-239 and is a regression from the previous behaviour.

The removed confirm_window logged 'Fenster laeuft jetzt bis' and 'der Lauf hat keines eroeffnet', and the ping twin still does (src/lib.rs:3525-3529). Operators lose the only evidence of whether a job actually opened a window, and a job that never opens one is invisible in the journal.

84b9957 and FINAL-CORRECTION.md say prediction 'limits ... have one definition' and that duplicated definitions were the cause. At HEAD the same limit still lives in three places with no named constant or derivation, so the documented 20-minute rule can drift between predictive_switch and projected_usage.

c3bd0fa says target reserve checks are shared across selection paths. Here the guard is applied separately in each caller instead of in the shared selection function, and two selection paths miss it. A target already inside its safety reserve can be chosen even when a safe one exists, and the predictive path then switches away again on the next tick.
The cap of 50 is not derived from the doubled-reserve admission rule. A value the code accepts as valid turns off features without any warning.

These are production payload fields with no consumer. SUBSCRIPTION.md presents subscriptionCheckedAt as part of the contract, yet nothing displays it, and the extra gate read costs file I/O on every dashboard request.

In the switch context the second clause about old usage is misleading. The refusal also rests on a stored verdict that never expires and is not rechecked during the switch, yet the message gives no hint how to re-verify (`claude-account usage` or the web refresh) or how to override with --no-check. This is misleading user-facing text.

This is the exact mechanism 84b9957 claims to fix ('An earlier caller clock could also discard a new measurement'), and it is fixed only in cached_levels (src/limit.rs:1235). A measurement written by another process (web refresh, CLI) between clock and read skips prediction or confirmation for that tick.

While a reader holds that lock, run_job_now fails with the false message 'Es laeuft bereits eine Aufgabe' (2870-2872) and automation_tick logs 'es laeuft bereits eine' and skips a due job (3434-3437). The run lock now has two meanings.

A profile saved while `claude auth status` reported no orgId is never verified. Its label stays 'Abo ungeprüft', a lost subscription is never detected (the fd494ef fix never takes effect for it), and log_problem 'Abo-Prüfung verworfen' repeats every 600 s per such profile (2295). The code has two truths for 'same account'.
FINAL-CORRECTION.md:13 and the commit claim 'Prediction reserve, lead, limits and horizon have one definition', but the age limit and 24 h caps are copies. Changing one leaves the others drifting.
Confirmation is now deferred to a later measurement. The comments misstate the behaviour and breach the repository's no-comment rule for touched code.
This is production payload without a consumer, and it is inconsistent with the payload's naming contract.
The lock now carries two meanings, so a list or panel refresh is reported as a running job and delays or fails a start.
A job removed or disabled in that window is recreated or re-enabled, and save_job_result then sees enabled=true and runs it. That is exactly what save_job_result's guard is meant to prevent.

A long job often triggers an auto-switch mid-run. The repeat job then sees B's already-used window as 'new' and reruns 15 minutes later. The removed confirm_window recorded the account active at completion, so this is a regression for repeating jobs.
After a switch, the new active account's unused window waits up to 15 minutes because of another quota's ping. Two records of the same ping disagree, and the commit message misstates the behaviour.
A permanent state becomes one journal line per minute, which contradicts the log_once policy and the commit's 'errors log only when they change'.
The operator log claims a ping was confirmed although none was sent, and with several accounts the lines cannot be attributed.
This is a dead guard that suggests a 60 s floor exists. Anyone tuning DEFAULT or MAX would believe a lower bound protects the API when the real floor is DEFAULT.

This is the same duplication class 84b9957 claims to remove ('reserve and lead definitions were duplicated'; FINAL-CORRECTION says horizon has one definition). Changing one site leaves predictive_switch and projected_usage disagreeing on staleness.
The three sites must agree, or an accepted server delay would be discarded on read or a retry_at ignored. There is no single definition and no stated unit derivation.

A measurement written by the web refresh or CLI between clock capture and read is ignored for that tick: prediction is skipped and the confirmation is delayed. The commit fixed only deduplicated_levels in src/limit.rs.
The test name claims identity sharing, but it can only fail if HashMap lookup breaks. A regression that keys claims by profile name would still pass.
This creates two truths for one decision parameter across consumers that share one budget and gate. It also breaks the rule that normal configuration belongs in config files.
This adds avoidable file I/O per profile on the web request path and extends the lock hold time shared by all usage consumers. The active profile could be loaded once per pass.

The merge base evaluated the active-profile closure lazily. Every hook process with auto_switch off now spawns `claude auth status` (src/lib.rs:4003) even in force mode, where the answer is fixed. That adds subprocess latency on the hook path, the cost the commit says it removed.

The Ursache layer 3 and FINAL-CORRECTION.md claim the tests exercise 'cheap hooks' and 'without launching an auth binary'. Reverting to active_profile_name_memoized keeps the test green, so the guard is unproven.

Example: aliases 'a' (stop 70) and 'b' (stop 98) on one quota at 75%. Only 'a' remains, so switch_target and best_other see Fit::No and the limit pause or hook can block although switching to 'b' is allowed. Which alias represents a non-active quota is never decided.

When gate.cached is absent (installs from before the gate, or a gate file that does not parse), a fresh cache written by a dropped alias is ignored. The quota then appears unknown, and minutes_to_pause becomes None. This twin is not covered by the Ursache layer 4.

Deleting that guard keeps this test and tests/cli.rs:3354 (identical resets_at in both samples) green. A slope across a reset (old window 10%, new window 30%) would then inflate the projection unnoticed.
FINAL-CORRECTION.md claims 'Prediction reserve, lead, limits and horizon have one definition', but this limit still has two copies that can drift, and no unit or derivation for it is stated.
One rule lives in two places, so a fix to one copy will not reach the other. Both copies also trim only the integer branch, not the date branch.
The commit's stated bug is a wrong Max label. When the two live fields disagree, the code can reproduce that wrong label, and no test would catch it.
For such accounts the subscription is never verified: they show 'Abo ungeprüft' forever, an expired subscription is never detected, and log_problem fires every 600 s.
Part of the guard can never take effect, and the error text 'muss endlich' describes a case that cannot occur. No test reaches lines 736-738.

The commit message of 84b9957 and FINAL-CORRECTION.md say the test proves both readiness guards. Only the idle guard (unique text at src/lib.rs:3256) is proven. The active guard can regress unnoticed, and the docs claim coverage that does not exist.
Deleting or weakening the 2x reserve guard on predictive targets would leave the test green. No other test covers a predictive target inside the reserve band (89-97%).

Comments misstate what the test proves. The multi-body sequence feature has no exercising caller left. The assertion message 'cached data must not confirm a new window' names a rule this assertion cannot catch.
The assertions cannot distinguish 'consumers share one measurement' from 'consumers got no measurement at all', so the sharing rule in the test name and in 36ea212 is not actually verified.

cold_measurement_reserve_switches_without_a_previous_sample (3408) and prediction_switches_early_only_with_a_safe_target (3354) silently depend on the defaults. They fail or change meaning on a machine or CI shell that exports these variables, and only auto_keeps_the_active_account_below_the_threshold (1962) pins one of them.

The fixture's last_run_at is now-1000, past MIN_RERUN_GAP_SECONDS = 900 (src/jobs.rs:21). Without the guard, ping_readiness returns Due (src/jobs.rs:303-309) and send_ping then bails with the identical text. Assert the full 'Fenster-Ping wartet: Bestätigung des letzten Pings steht aus' and the absence of 'Fenster-Ping faellig'.
The guard looks like evidence but cannot detect a confirmation path that sends a request. Enable ping in the fixture (as tests/cli.rs:3672 does) so the assertion reaches the ping path.

Suppose another consumer (watcher, web refresh or CLI) writes a measurement in the next second between clock and read. Prediction is then skipped for that tick and an early switch is lost. The ping confirmation stays pending one extra tick, which blocks pings longer. 84b9957 fixed exactly this pattern only in cached_levels_for (src/limit.rs:1219).
The branch can never take effect and misstates the storage layout to maintainers. Use the accounts path directly.
The accounts are saved; they lack an active subscription. The user-facing text misstates the state and points the user to the wrong fix. Same class as web/app.js:107-108.
The user already has saved accounts. The real blocker is that none has an active subscription, so the text sends them to save a duplicate account. Same class as web/app.js:270.
The default can never take effect with the current backend and is a second definition of the stale threshold that disagrees with both backend values. Neither copy was derived from the other.

When a read overlaps, automation_tick's try_lock (lib.rs:3434-3436) logs 'es laeuft bereits eine' and skips the job start, and run_job_now bails with 'Es laeuft bereits eine Aufgabe' (lib.rs:2870-2871), although no job is running. A read path now contends with the run lock.

For such profiles, inactive-subscription protection can never fire, the label stays 'Abo ungeprüft', and 'Abo-Prüfung verworfen' is logged via log_problem every 10 minutes (lib.rs:2295). There are two truths for the same account identity.

This is a twin of 36ea212's 'callers lacked shared single-flight reservation', now for the profile endpoint. A 429 seen by one path does not pause the other, so identity resolution and subscription checks can keep hitting a throttled endpoint.

Logs at lib.rs:2302-2305 ('Abo von X nicht bestätigt: Auslastungs-API …') and lib.rs:3942 ('Live-Login liess sich nicht zuordnen: Auslastungs-API …') name the wrong endpoint, which misleads diagnosis of which API is throttling.
Commit 84b9957 claims that reserve, lead, limits and horizon have one definition. These copies can drift independently.
These are production payload fields without a consumer. subscriptionCheckedAt also costs an extra gate read per profile on every dashboard poll.
There are two truths for the same measurement. With aliases, only the fetching alias's usage.json is updated, so a gate read error silently serves a different alias's older per-name value.
84b9957 claims the repeated-error siblings were fixed, but only the ping-idle and confirmation logs got log_once. These twins flood the journal, which the repo's own log_once design intends to avoid.
A single corrupt store-wide budget file stops all usage measurement and therefore all switching until someone deletes it by hand. No exit or recovery exists.
This adds a possible auth-status subprocess to the hook request path in cases where the answer does not depend on it.
The service, CLI, web and hook processes can run with different values, so target admission and prediction disagree between consumers. docs/usage-gate.md only asks users to 'set them consistently'.
